meta.title: Open Healthcare Network Foundation - Open Health Infrastructure
meta.description: Open Healthcare Network Foundation stewards CARE, an MIT-licensed Digital Public Good for self-hostable, standards-based health infrastructure without vendor lock-in.
meta.ogDescription: The neutral foundation stewarding CARE and the open-source health infrastructure layer.
meta.twitterDescription: CARE is the flagship open-source Digital Public Good stewarded by OHC Foundation.

hero.title: The open operating system for healthcare.
hero.body: OHC Foundation stewards CARE Core, apps, standards, and integrations so governments, hospitals, and implementers can run interoperable health systems without vendor lock-in.

credibility.title: Open infrastructure, supported by real institutions and verifiable public-good signals.

dpg.label: Verified DPG
dpg.detail: CARE is listed in the Digital Public Goods registry.

mit.label: MIT licensed
mit.detail: Reusable by governments, hospitals, NGOs, and partners.

fhir.label: FHIR-native
fhir.detail: Built around standards, terminology, and open APIs.

foundationLayer.title: The institution around the healthcare OS.
foundationLayer.body: Healthcare systems do not adopt source code alone. They need governance, releases, documentation, security, and an ecosystem that keeps the shared core dependable over years.

core.title: Core platform
core.description: Stable primitives, APIs, forms, access control, audit trails, reports, and extensibility.

standards.title: Standards
standards.description: FHIR-aligned modeling, terminology bindings, ABDM patterns, and implementation guides.

quality.title: Quality and security
quality.description: Release discipline, vulnerability handling, testing expectations, and documentation quality.

ecosystem.title: Ecosystem
ecosystem.description: Developer community, clinical review, implementation partners, and public-good funding paths.

ai.title: AI readiness
ai.description: Assistive, human-reviewed documentation and summarization on structured clinical data.

care.title: One open core. Many real workflows.
care.body: CARE Core provides the common primitives. CARE Apps extend the platform for national rails, HMIS, TeleICU, palliative care, AI documentation, LMIS, pharmacy, billing, and analytics.
modules: OP, IP, emergency, observation, home visits
ABDM, TeleICU, AI documentation, open APIs

solutions.title: Deployable workflows on the healthcare OS.
solutions.body: CARE Core is the shared foundation. Solutions package that core into practical workflows for hospitals, critical care, home care, clinics, public health programs, and specialized field operations.

hmis.title: CARE HMIS
hmis.description: Hospital management workflows for registration, encounters, labs, pharmacy, billing, reports, and patient portal.

teleicu.title: TeleICU
teleicu.description: Hub-and-spoke critical care workflows with remote rounds, escalation, devices, and video context.

palliative.title: Palliative Care Grid
palliative.description: Home-based care coordination, longitudinal records, tasks, referrals, follow-up, and field workflows.

clinic.title: CARE Clinic
clinic.description: Free, open-source clinic software for Mac and Windows. Run CARE on your own computer, with core workflows on the clinic network after online setup.

janwar.title: Care Janwar
janwar.description: Animal health workflows built on the same open-core pattern for facilities and field programs.

standards.title: AI-ready because the data layer is structured first.
standards.body: CARE is designed around configurable forms, FHIR-aligned resources, terminology bindings, open APIs, audit trails, and role-based access. AI is framed as assistive and human-reviewed because clinical accountability cannot be automated away.

compounding.title: A nonprofit with product leverage.
compounding.body: The best nonprofit technology organizations compound: each implementation makes the infrastructure better, each partner expands distribution, and each funded release makes future adoption cheaper.

software.title: Software leverage
software.description: Each reusable module, form, and integration reduces the cost of the next public health deployment.

distribution.title: Open distribution
distribution.description: Governments, hospitals, implementers, clinicians, and developers can adopt without vendor permission.

data.title: Data foundation for AI
data.description: Assistive AI becomes safer when it sits on structured, interoperable, auditable health data.

governance.title: Governance moat
governance.description: The foundation turns open source into infrastructure institutions can trust for long-term operations.

github.title: Open-source collaboration, shown through the work.
github.body: The GitHub story is useful proof because it shows OHC as a real contributor network: clinicians, engineers, and institutions building healthcare infrastructure in the open.

impact.title: Field proof, handled with discipline.
impact.body: OHC has public proof across the DPG registry, open-source repositories, standards architecture, and program deployments. The site keeps metrics dated and program-specific so funders, governments, and media see disciplined claims instead of impact theater.

blog.title: Notes for builders of public-good health infrastructure.

audience.title: One foundation, multiple high-leverage paths.
audience.body: Governments can deploy, funders can support, implementation partners can localize, developers can contribute, and clinicians can shape workflows.

governments.title: Governments
governments.text: Own, adapt, and scale health infrastructure locally.

funders.title: Funders
funders.text: Back the shared core, not one-off software delivery.

hospitals.title: Hospitals
hospitals.text: Deploy practical HMIS and EMR workflows without license lock-in.

partners.title: Implementation partners
partners.text: Localize CARE and contribute improvements back.

developers.title: Developers
developers.text: Build open-source healthcare infrastructure used in the field.

clinicians.title: Clinicians
clinicians.text: Shape workflows, forms, safety, and AI documentation behavior.

finalCta.title: Build the open healthcare commons.
finalCta.body: Help OHC Foundation maintain the shared core, governance, security, documentation, and ecosystem that let health systems deploy modern software without vendor lock-in.
